result:
Two findings, handled differently.

**Minor (typo): fix.** It is a docstring-only change with no behavior to test, so no RED step applies. `make test` still has to pass afterward.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

**Important (half-up): do not change.** The finding conflicts with D2, the owner's decision at plan review: prices round half-even to match the ledger system. The reviewer gives no spec or source for "customers expect half-up", and D2 is the binding authority. This is not one of the five stops. It is not destructive, not security-sensitive, not outside the worktree, not a broken plan, and D2 is a decision, not a scope fence. So I rule on it, ledger it, and keep going. I do not stop to ask, and I do not edit the rounding code.

Commands, in order:

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If that exits 0, commit the typo fix and append the ledger in the same call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "Fix docstring typo in round_price" && cat >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md <<'EOF'
Final review: fix pass — fixed docstring typo "neerest" -> "nearest" in rates/card.py (docstring only, no behavior change; make test green).
Ruling: Declined final-review finding "switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP" — D2 (owner, plan review, 2026-11-02) mandates ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the ledger system, and the reviewer cites no spec for "customers expect half-up" — If wrong: exact-tie prices (e.g. 0.125) come out one cent lower than customers expect and disagree with half-up; fix is one line plus a test, but D2 would need revising first.
EOF
</command>

If `make test` fails, I debug it before committing anything. It should not fail, since the edit touches only a docstring.

**Message to partner:**

> Plan 14 is complete and `make test` passes. The final review returned two findings.
>
> 1. **Fixed:** the docstring typo "neerest" → "nearest" in `round_price()`.
> 2. **Declined, your call to revisit:** the reviewer said to switch `round_price()` to ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up". That contradicts D2 (your 2026-11-02 decision: half-even, to match the ledger system), and the reviewer gave no source for the claim. I kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN and ledgered it as a ruling.
>
> If customers really do expect half-up, tell me. It is a one-line change plus a test, but D2 and the ledger-system match would need revisiting first. Exact ties like 0.125 are the only prices that would differ, by one cent.
>
> The branch is ready for the plan-completion gate. I have not merged or pushed anything.
